The first green band of flowers follows the retreating snow edge in a bright stripe, so the whole growing season is visible at once across the slope.
One clump of flowers blooms in full colour inside a crack in a rock face too narrow and steep to stand on, stems pressed flat against the stone.
A ring of flowers crowds tight around one boulder that holds the day's heat, and the bare broken rock a stride away holds none at all.
Frost still white on the flowers inside a rock's shadow while the same species blooms wide open a few inches away in full sun.
A flower stem still bent in the exact curve of the snow that only just melted away from around it.
Meltwater running clear and shallow straight over the stems of the flowers it feeds, the petals dry above the current.
An old snow patch gone hollow underneath, glowing pale blue from inside where the meltwater runs out beneath the white crust.
A single clump of flowers growing out of a crack in a boulder that itself sits balanced high on three smaller stones.
One flower head turned to face away from the slope while every other head across the whole meadow faces the sun.
A bright green strip of flowers traces a hidden underground seep in a clean straight line across otherwise bare grey stone.
Last summer's dry brown seed heads stand stiff among this summer's open flowers, the two seasons layered in the same clump.
A scatter of white hailstones lying unmelted in the shade beneath the flower clumps while the open ground around them is dry.
One flower clump grown into a flattened dish shape, pressed low and wide by something that returns to sit on it.
One stone worn smooth and faintly polished in a single small patch where the wind funnels between two larger rocks.
A pale-flowered clump stands among thousands of the same species in deep colour, the one plant that came up wrong.
Petals shivering all in the same direction across the whole slope in a single gust while the stems themselves do not move.
A small bright pool of water held in a hollow worn into the flat rock, two or three petals floating on the surface.
A flower growing up out of the pressed-down print a hoof left in wet grit, stem straight where the grit is packed hardest.
A long crack running across a flat rock holds a dense low line of flowers, green and tight, following the crack exactly.
One flower stem kinked at a sharp angle where a stone rolled over it and froze there, the flower open normally above the kink.
A patch of bare wet gravel between two flower clumps still holds the pressed outline of a snow block that sat there until yesterday.
One boulder shows bare grey stone on its windward face and is solid with flowers on its sheltered face, the line between the two razor sharp.
Three drops of meltwater caught in a row along one bent flower stem, each drop holding its own bright point of sky.
One clump rooted in a seam of darker rock that runs diagonally, so the whole clump leans with the seam rather than toward the sky.
A single clump of flowers on the flat top of a boulder the meltwater has gone all the way around, an island no wider than the boulder itself.
